description: Class-A1: slash-collapse spelling equivalence in write_guard's BASH channel. Pre-fix, ``_hook_utils.normalize_bash_path`` did NOT collapse a redundant ``.//`` / ``.///`` current-directory prefix, nor strip the leading ``/`` left after substituting ``$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`` in ``$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR//<protected>``. The OS resolves all of these to the same protected file (``.//.claude/settings.json`` is ``.claude/settings.json``), but the string-prefix check ran against the un-normalized spelling and missed it, so a Bash redirect / tee write into a protected zone was ALLOWED. The Write/Edit channel (``normalize_path``) already collapsed ``.//`` pre-fix, so this class is bash-channel-specific. The fix is a canonicalize-or-fail-closed chokepoint — ``replace("\\","/")`` at the top of both normalisers + ``lstrip("/")`` after each env-var strip and the Bash ``./`` strip — so every slash spelling folds to the canonical relative path before the protected-zone check. This is the regression gate that keeps the class fixed; it is paired with the code fix. NOTE (documented known-limit, intentionally NOT a row here): a BARE leading ``//`` (``//.claude/...``) correctly stays ALLOWED — it names a filesystem-root-absolute path, a different file — and the backslash-separator spelling is a Windows-host concern, untestable on POSIX.
documented_in: tests/test_write_guard.py::TestClassA1ChokepointEndToEnd (Class-A1 path canonicalize-or-fail-closed chokepoint, end-to-end through the hook)
